critique: The black background and warm yellow/orange palette are appropriate, and the blast shifts rightward between 0.01 and 0.08. However, it remains a dense, rounded overlapping-particle cloud at both times. It has no readable forward flame wedge, pointed leading edge, separated fast sparks, or hot near-white ignition core; motion is primarily a uniform translation of the blob rather than a directional explosive spread.

suggestions.why: Collapse the wide emitter volume so the flash originates from a tight muzzle point instead of beginning as a circular cloud.
Collapse the emitter height with the X size to establish a concentrated source for a directional wedge.
Introduce substantial forward speed variation so the burst resolves into a tapered stream of leading particles and trailing sparks rather than translating as one compact mass.
Reduce oversized overlapping particle discs, allowing the directional spread and spark structure to read clearly.
Push the main flash toward a hot near-white/yellow core, closer to an explosive muzzle ignition than the current uniform orange-yellow blob.
